people/bixel: bixel built the kahu-tok language. the work began in the early generations after the first descent, when the survivors who had carried the bastard tongue down out of the bunkers needed a shared speech that could grow with the new community.
people/hanna-miskinnis: hanna miskinnis discovered biological immortality. her research group, working in the years before the fracture, developed the telomere intervention that allowed the human body to halt the cellular aging process.
people/mara: mara did not found the zou-esh. the order existed before her, going back at least to the messengers of the age of tapestry who spread the legend of the mountain that breathes. what mara did was become the most famous and most prolific zou-esh on record.
people/ston: ston is named in the kahu record. the records currently available do not yet fix the role, the dates, or the era. this entry is a placeholder for the figure and will be expanded as records are recovered.
people/the-bunker-survivors: the bunker survivors are the surviving populations of the deep mountain bunkers in the cascade arc who rode out the dark century underground and became the founding generation of the kahu. they are the ancestors. everything the kahu now are descends, in part, from what these people survived and how they survived it.
people/the-cat-farmers: the cat-farmers are the small farming community living below the caldera who, when mara's zou-esh expedition found them during the age of bloom, were in possession of the serval-cougar hybrid cats that would become the kahu cats.
people/the-longs: the longs are the pre-collapse ultra-wealthy who monopolized the miskinnis longevity intervention in the years before the fracture. they are the immortal elite who took the technology that hanna miskinnis had refused to use and sealed themselves inside arcologies.
people/the-yamantau-descendants: the yamantau descendants are the bunker descendants of the russian yamantau facility who crossed the bering ice bridge in a multi-generational migration and arrived at tora vyl drak during the late age of tapestry.
places/hart-ston: hart-ston is the active volcanic cone that sits within the caldera. the name in kahu-tok reads heart-stone. the cone is sacred to the kahu. it is also the source of the residual heat that keeps them alive.
places/hart-wata: hart-wata is the great lake at the center of tora vyl drak. the name in kahu-tok reads heart-water. it is the kahu's primary freshwater source and the geographic center of life inside the caldera.
places/hot-kasa: hot-kasa is the principal settlement of the kahu. the name in kahu-tok reads hot-house, the warmth. approximately one hundred and twenty thousand kahu live here, roughly forty-three percent of the total population.
places/komi-wata: komi-wata is the river of sun-tera, the south quadrant of tora vyl drak. the name carries wata, the kahu-tok root for water. it is the working water of the breadbasket, the river the south quadrant's agriculture is built around.
places/mara-skol: mara-skol is the zou-esh training institution. the name in kahu-tok reads mara-school. the school is located at the gate, the chokepoint where the long climb meets the nu-tera plateau, the place where mara died.
places/nu-tera: nu-tera is the plateau that wraps the southern flank of tora vyl drak. the name in kahu-tok reads new-land. the plateau sits just above five thousand feet, on the safe side of the peli-shen spore line by a margin of dozens to hundreds of feet depending on the season and the year.
places/ol-tri-shen: ol-tri shen is the forest preserve at the heart of the wilds, the north quadrant of tora vyl drak. the name in kahu-tok reads old-tree life. it is the kahu's longest-running deliberate non-cultivation and the closest thing inside the caldera to ancient ecology.
places/sun-tera: sun-tera is the south quadrant of the caldera. the name in kahu-tok reads sun-land. it is the kahu's principal agricultural zone inside tora vyl drak proper and the source of most of the caldera's food.
places/the-gate: the gate is the chokepoint where the long climb tops out onto the nu-tera plateau. it is the only ascent path from the world below the spore line to the kahu sanctuary above. the long climb is narrow throughout and impassable in winter. the gate is where the climb ends and the plateau begins.
places/the-great-western-sea: the great western sea is the toxic inland sea created by the 2075 cascadia impact. it sits west of the cascade arc, where the willamette valley used to be. it is one of the major geographic features of the kahu's world and the western boundary of the territory the zou-esh operate within.
places/the-hearth: the hearth is the west quadrant of the caldera, the part of the basin nearest to the residual magma chamber beneath tora vyl drak. it holds the geothermal grid, the principal settlement of hot-kasa, and most of the kahu's industrial and infrastructure systems.
places/the-long-climb: the long climb is the narrow ascent path from the lowlands to the nu-tera plateau. it is the only land approach to tora vyl drak from the world below the peli-shen spore line. anyone who reaches the kahu reaches them by this route, the gate at its top, and the stone climb above that.
places/the-stone-climb: ston-klimb is the spiral walkway cut into the rock face that connects the nu-tera plateau to the caldera floor of tora vyl drak. the english rendering is the stone climb. its name in kahu-tok reads stone-climb, directly.
places/the-wilds: the wilds are the north quadrant of the caldera. the quadrant is mostly unsettled. it holds the ol-tri shen forest preserve and the kahu's principal contact with non-cultivated ecology inside the rim.
places/the-wrap-around: the wrap-around is the northern shaded flank of the nu-tera plateau. it wraps the northern face of tora vyl drak's rim around to meet the broader plateau on its eastern and western edges. it is the cat-kahu's territory.
places/tora-vyl-drak: tora vyl drak is the eighteen-mile volcanic caldera in the cascade range that has been the kahu sanctuary since the first descent in 2283 ad. the name reads, in importance-first kahu-tok, hope, call, last: the hope of the last call. the kahu named it for what it is.
events/the-caldera-shudder: the caldera shudder is the violent subterranean seismic warning that struck beneath tora vyl drak in approximately 4525 ad, one hundred years before the present.
events/the-first-descent: the first descent is the event by which the kahu became the kahu.
events/the-fracture: the fracture is the event that ended the world before. on november 10, 2075, at approximately 07:33 utc, the combined nuclear arsenals of the united states, russia, and china executed humanity's final act of global coordination.
events/the-great-eruption: the great eruption is the geological event that formed tora vyl drak. it occurred in approximately 2133 ad, fifty-eight years after the fracture and the cascadia impact of 2075.
events/the-great-silence: the great silence is the kahu term for the global electromagnetic pulse that ended the age of electricity in the moments of the fracture. the silence happened in the same minutes as the impacts, on november 10, 2075.
events/the-leveling: the leveling is the event by which the surface survivors of the fracture took back from the longs the ability to ever rule the surface again.
events/the-schism: the schism is the unfolding theological and medical disagreement within the kahu about how much biological intervention is appropriate. it is the central live conflict of the present moment in tora vyl drak.
eras/age-of-bloom: the age of bloom is the twelve-hundred-year golden age of kahu civilization. it spans approximately 2700 to 3925 ad, from the end of the founding work of the tapestry through the long quiet stretch during which the kahu way of life reached its apex. nearly half of the kahu's recorded history is the bloom.
eras/age-of-endura: the age of endura is the modern era of the kahu. it began in approximately 3925 ad, when the age of bloom, the twelve-hundred-year golden age of kahu civilization, gave way to a longer and quieter time of strain. the kahu of the present, in 4625 ad, live seven hundred years into the age of endura.
eras/age-of-tapestry: the age of tapestry is the founding era of the kahu civilization. it spans approximately 2283 to 2700 ad, from the first descent into the caldera through the four centuries of construction, language-building, and institutional formation that produced the kahu world.
eras/the-dark-century: the dark century is the era between the fracture and the first descent. it spans approximately 2075 to 2283 ad, two hundred and eight years. it is the era before the kahu, the era during which the people who would become the kahu's ancestors survived underground, watched the surface, and waited.
concepts/fas-big: the fas-big is the zou-esh's unsanctioned rite of challenge. the order does not authorize it, but the order recognizes it, and the order accounts for it: a zou-esh who undertakes the fas-big takes an automatic two hits in the three hits system, which leaves them one short of the limit of three.
concepts/importance-first-syntax: importance-first syntax is the foundational syntactic principle of kahu-tok. the most important element of a sentence leads. emphasis, focus, and the speaker's actual point are visible from the first word.
concepts/kahu: kahu is the word for the kahu people, the inhabitants of tora vyl drak and the plateau of nu-tera. it is also the word for a kahu, a single community of any size from a family-scale household through a sub-community to the entire population of approximately two hundred and seventy-eight thousand.
concepts/kau-esh: the kau-esh are the little kahu. the term covers two overlapping groups: those who are in zou-esh training but have not yet completed it, and those who began the training and did not finish, the washouts. kau reads as a diminutive, a smaller or incomplete form, set against the full kahu.
concepts/peli-shen: peli-shen is the fungus that has rendered the lowlands lethal. the name in kahu-tok reads danger-life. it is the reason the kahu live above five thousand feet.
concepts/the-bastard-tongue: tok-peles is the simplified english-creole patois spoken by the bunker survivors of the dark century. the name in kahu-tok reads place-talk, indicating the language's character as a localized survival speech rather than an inherited formal tongue. the english rendering is the bastard tongue.
concepts/the-bixel-1000: the bixel 1000 is the approximately one thousand engineered roots and stems that form the foundational core of the kahu-tok language. it is bixel's deliberate design from the early age of tapestry, the architecture of the language at the lexical level.
concepts/the-cascade: the cascade is the volcanic arc that runs the length of what was, before the fracture, the pacific northwest of the united states and the canadian province of british columbia. the arc holds tora vyl drak. the kahu call the range the bones of the cascade or simply the cascade.
concepts/the-creeping-dark: the creeping dark is the kahu name for the slow neurotoxic descent caused by accumulating peli-shen exposure. it is what happens to the mind of a person who lives below five thousand feet.
concepts/the-deliberate-absences: the deliberate absences are the words kahu-tok does not have, and was built not to have. the language has no word for money. none for debt, for rent, for interest. it has hav, which means to hold, to carry, to have-with-you, and it has no word for own. the gap is not an oversight of a small vocabulary.
concepts/the-dual-mandate: the dual mandate is the formal shape of the zou-esh mission. the order's work in the world below has two halves, and the order names them as two.
concepts/the-five-filters-of-uniqueness: the five filters of uniqueness are the five conditions, geological and human, that together make tora vyl drak the only sanctuary of its kind on the post-fracture earth. each filter is necessary; none alone is sufficient. all five had to apply at the same place at the same time for a civilization to be possible.
concepts/the-goldilocks-filter: the goldilocks filter is the band of elevation that the kahu survive inside. it is high enough that peli-shen cannot complete its life cycle, and low enough that human life remains viable. the kahu live in the narrow window between the spore and the cold.
concepts/the-great-devaluation: the great devaluation is the kahu term for the decades of institutional decay, information warfare, and environmental degradation that preceded the fracture. it is, in kahu reckoning, the world that broke before the world broke.
concepts/the-hyper-winter: the hyper-winter is the kahu term for the years of permanent twilight and freezing temperatures that followed the fracture. it is the climate condition that killed nine in ten of the impact survivors and that defined the conditions of the bunker survival from which the kahu's ancestors emerged.
concepts/the-kahu-cat-partnership: the kahu cat partnership is the working relationship between a zou-esh and their cat across the full arc of training, active service, and post-active life. it is one of the deepest institutional patterns in the kahu order and one of the central facts of zou-esh life.
concepts/the-kahu-cats: the kahu cats are the serval-cougar hybrid cats bred over approximately a thousand years by the cat-kahu, from the original lineage that arrived in tora vyl drak with mara's diplomatic mission during the age of bloom. they are the partners of the zou-esh in the field.
concepts/the-last-walk: the last walk is the gravest penalty in kahu justice. it is exile. the condemned is escorted by zou-esh beyond the rim of tora vyl drak, given tools, seeds, and knowledge, and left in the world below to live or die on their own.
concepts/the-mountain-that-breathes: the mountain that breathes is the kahu's geothermal plume as it appeared to distant survivor pockets across the dark century. the kahu themselves call the source of the plume hart-ston, the sacred volcanic cone within the caldera.
concepts/the-naming: every kahu carries one name, and no two living kahu carry the same one.
concepts/the-rebirth-naming: the rebirth naming is a purist practice surrounding the release of names at death.
concepts/the-three-hits: the three hits are a tracking system internal to the zou-esh. the order counts something in threes against each of its members, and the count carries consequence. the fas-big, the order's unsanctioned rite of challenge, carries an automatic two hits, which places a single fas-big one short of the limit.
concepts/the-three-waves-of-extinction: the three waves of extinction is the kahu framework for understanding how the human population collapsed across the dark century. the kahu's account of the fracture's aftermath identifies three distinct waves, each of which killed a substantial fraction of the survivors of the previous wave.
concepts/the-trinity-lock: the trinity lock is the personalized three-stage mechanism that opens a zou-esh's jefe-tri bow into its broken-down close-quarters configuration. each zou-esh's trinity lock is unique to them. it cannot be opened by anyone else without specific knowledge of that zou-esh's individual lock pattern.
concepts/the-white-zone: the white zone is the elevation above roughly five thousand feet that is effectively free of peli-shen. it is the clean air, the safe ground, the band the kahu live inside. its name marks the absence of the fungus: above the line, the spore does not hold.
concepts/warden: warden is the kahu's central decision-support system. it is a continent-scale biological supercomputer, realized during the age of bloom, that models the kahu's agriculture, infrastructure, ecology, demographics, and the long arc of consequences for the choices the kahu make.
organizations/the-cat-kahu: the cat-kahu are the kahu order responsible for the breeding, training, and stewardship of the kahu cats. they are a small lineage-based community living on the wrap-around of the nu-tera plateau, the northern shaded flank of tora vyl drak's rim.
organizations/the-council-of-the-tapestr: the council of the tapestry is the formal structure of kahu governance. where the council is the everyday name for the integrating body that deliberates on caldera-wide questions, the council of the tapestry is its formal shape: a bicameral assembly with two chambers, an executive triad, and a separate judicial body.
organizations/the-council: the council is the central institutional structure of kahu governance. it is the body that deliberates on caldera-wide questions and integrates the recommendations of warden into kahu decision-making.
organizations/the-kahu-silth: the kahu-silth are the order of bio-artisans who grow, shape, and heal the kahu's living garments. the name is built from silth, the kahu-tok root for weaving and fiber, and kahu, the community. they are the weaving-kahu, though the work is closer to biology than to weaving as the old world understood it.
organizations/the-pathfinders: the pathfinders are the judicial council of the kahu, known in kahu-tok as tru-tapi. there are three of them, drawn from three different parts of kahu life so that no single perspective holds the whole of justice.
organizations/the-three-speakers: the three speakers are the executive triad of kahu governance, the small body that articulates the consensus of the two chambers of the council of the tapestry and gives it a voice.
organizations/the-warden-tenders: the warden-tenders are the kahu order responsible for the living systems of tora vyl drak. they are an apothecary-priest hybrid. their work is upstream of every kahu decision that depends on biotech, ecological management, or the consultation of warden.
organizations/zou-esh: the zou-esh are the scholar-warrior order of the kahu. their work has two faces. they defend the gate, the chokepoint at the top of the long climb, against any incursion from below.
objects/air-klin: air-klin is the respiratory biome inoculation administered to zou-esh before deep or sustained operations below the peli-shen spore line. the name in kahu-tok reads clean-air or air-clean. it is part of the zou-esh's layered defenses against the fungus that has rendered the lowlands lethal.
objects/jefe-tri: jefe-tri is the personalized bow of the zou-esh. each weapon is unique to its owner. it is designed, crafted, and recrafted by the zou-esh across the years of their training. by the time the zou-esh graduates to active service, the bow is the physical record of their own development as a fighter.
objects/klin-soma: klin-soma is the bio-monitoring undersuit worn against the skin under the zou-esh's other layers. the name in kahu-tok reads clean-body or clean-living-body, indicating the suit's continuous diagnostic function. it tracks the zou-esh's body state across the entire duration of operations.
objects/living-textiles: living textiles are the kahu's living garments, grown and shaped by the kahu-silth. in a world without microchips, where biology does the work that machines once did, cloth is not inert. a living textile is a system. it monitors the body, protects it, heals it, and adapts to it over the life of the garment.
objects/mirar-sin-ropa: mirar-sin-ropa is the passive camouflage cloak of the zou-esh. the name in kahu-tok reads see-without-clothes or no-see-clothes, indicating the function. the cloak makes a stationary zou-esh extremely difficult to distinguish from the terrain they are sitting in.
objects/soma-ropa: soma-ropa is the layered suit of the zou-esh taken as a whole. the name in kahu-tok reads body-clothes. it is the umbrella term that covers the three principal garment layers: the klin-soma bio-monitoring undersuit worn against the skin, the ston-ropa shear-thickening armor cloth that forms the outer shirts and pants,…
objects/ston-ropa: ston-ropa is the shear-thickening cloth that forms the zou-esh's shirts and pants. the name in kahu-tok reads rock-clothes. the cloth is thin and looks like ordinary clothing. under slow pressure it yields; a finger can push into it as into any garment. under sudden impact it resists like solid rock.
objects/ston-shen: ston-shen is the chemosynthetic lichen-bacteria paste that sustained the kahu's ancestors through the dark century. the name in kahu-tok reads rock-life. it is the food that kept humanity alive during the long underground, between the failure of the bunker rations and the first descent into the caldera.
objects/the-cloth-mask: the cloth mask is the filtering respiratory protection of the zou-esh's kit. it covers the nose and mouth. its function is to filter peli-shen spores at the concentrations a zou-esh encounters below the five thousand foot spore line. the kahu-tok name for the mask is open canon.
objects/the-gloves: the gloves are the hand equipment of the zou-esh's kit. their distinguishing function is that they adhere to the zou-esh's weapon, the jefe-tri bow and its broken-down close-quarters components, allowing controlled retention through complex movements and clean transitions from one configuration to another without the…
objects/the-zou-kit: the zou-kit is the standard field equipment of the zou-esh. the kit is the outward sign of the order. it is also the technological foundation that allows the order to operate below the peli-shen spore line and to defend the gate against threats arriving from there. the kit is entirely living cloth and biotech.
language/drak: drak is the kahu-tok word for last. it is one of the foundational roots of the bixel 1000. its placement in the construction tora vyl drak is the trailing modifier in importance-first order: hope, call, last. the last call. drak qualifies the call as the final one, the ultimate attempt, the terminal opportunity.
language/hart: hart is the kahu-tok word for heart. it is one of the foundational roots of the bixel 1000.
language/hot: hot is the kahu-tok word for warm or heated. it is one of the foundational roots of the bixel 1000.
language/kaelith: kaelith is the kahu name for the bonded cat. the animals are descended from serval-cougar hybrids that arrived with the cat-farmers on mara's founding diplomatic mission, and they have been bred and held ever since by the cat-kahu. the name is used for the cat as a kind.
language/kahu-tok: kahu-tok is the kahu's name for their own language. the compound reads kahu-talk in literal kahu-tok order. the engineered replacement language for tok-peles, the bastard tongue of the bunker era. designed by bixel during the early age of tapestry. its master lexicon, the thousand words bixel set down, is the mil-tok.
language/kahu: kahu is the foundational word of the kahu-tok language and of the kahu world. it means a community of people. it is used at every scale: the family unit of ten to twelve people, the larger sub-community of fifty to sixty, the entire population of approximately two hundred and seventy-eight thousand.
language/kasa: kasa is the kahu-tok word for house, home, or dwelling. it is one of the foundational roots of the bixel 1000.
language/kia-vyl: !kia-vyl is the kahu-tok imperative construction meaning "live!" as a command. it is most famously the inscription scrawled into the rock at the gate, the last command mara gave as she ordered her zou-esh team to continue without her while she fought the raiders alone.
language/mara: mara, written in lowercase, is the kahu-tok word for a shield, and by extension for that which defends. it is an eponym: the common noun was taken from the name of mara, the legendary zou-esh who died holding the gate against raiders. the proper name, written mara and underlined, is the woman.
language/micasu: micasu is the kahu-tok word for welcome. it is one of the organic accretions to the language, words that entered the lexicon from the bunker populations the zou-esh brought home rather than from bixel's engineered core.
language/no: no is the kahu-tok word for no. it is the answer to a yes-or-no question and the grammatical negation that turns a statement around. it is one of the foundational words of the kahu-tok core.
language/peli-shen: peli-shen is the kahu-tok word for the radiotrophic fungus that has rendered the post-fracture lowlands lethal. the literal reading of the compound is "danger-life," from peli (danger) and shen (life).
language/peli: peli is the kahu-tok word for danger. it is one of the foundational roots of the bixel 1000. it functions both as a noun (a danger, the concept of danger) and as an interjection used in shortened form as a warning exclamation.
language/sav: sav is the kahu-tok verb for to know. it comes from the spanish saber, carried in by the hearth-tongue speakers of the founding generations and regularized by bixel into the engineered core.
language/shen: shen is the kahu-tok word for life. it is one of the foundational roots of the bixel 1000 and one of the productive compounding roots of the language.
language/silth: silth is the kahu-tok root for weaving, fiber, and the shaping of living textile. it is pronounced "seelth." it is a bound root, which means it appears inside compounds rather than standing alone in ordinary speech.
language/somohapian: a somohapian is the woven memory of a single life, kept with warden. it is the record of one kahu member, added to across the years they live: the days worth keeping, the work done, the people held, the things learned and lost. it is not a list of deeds and not a tally of property, which the kahu do not keep anyway.
language/ston: ston is the kahu-tok word for rock or stone. it is one of the foundational roots of the bixel 1000, and one of the most productive compounding roots in the language.
language/sun: sun is the kahu-tok word for the sun. it is one of the foundational roots of the bixel 1000, carrying direct english inheritance through the bunker speech of the dark century.
language/tera: tera is the kahu-tok word for land, ground, or earth. it is one of the foundational roots of the bixel 1000.
language/tok-peles: tok-peles is the kahu-tok term for the simplified english-creole patois spoken by the bunker survivors during the dark century. the english rendering is the bastard tongue.
language/tonal-tense: kahu-tok marks time by tone. a verb does not change its form to move between past, present, and future. it changes its tone. the same base word, spoken three ways, carries all three times.
language/tora: tora is the kahu-tok word for hope. it is one of the foundational roots of the bixel 1000.
language/vyl: vyl is the kahu-tok word for call. it is one of the foundational roots of the bixel 1000.
language/wan-slip-bak-ya-sem: wan-slip-bak, ya-sem is a kahu-tok idiom for the kind of memory that has not yet become the past. literally it is "one sleep back, now-same": a thing that happened a sleep ago and still feels like now.
language/wata: wata is the kahu-tok word for water. it is one of the foundational roots of the bixel 1000.
language/zou-esh: zou-esh is the kahu-tok word for the scholar-warrior order of the kahu. it is used both for the order collectively and, in the singular, for an individual member. "a zou-esh," "the zou-esh," and "the order" are all valid in english renderings; the kahu-tok form does not formally distinguish.
